text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Elections divide the General Labour Confederation after Lebanon's civil war failed to split it. The result: One union for the government and one for the opposition.
- Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri promises to support agro-industrialists.
- Opposition Christian MP Nassib Lahoud calls on parliamentary deputies to reject an eight-month proposed extension of parliament's mandate.
- Lebanon's delegate to the United Nations calls for the resumption of peace talks on the Madrid conference basis.
- Preparations under way for the Pope's visit to Lebanon in May.
- Workers at Casino du Liban to start an open-ended strike on Saturday.
- Bank of Lebanon issues certificates of deposits dated April 25 worth 76 billion pounds ($48.6 million).
- Israel shells south Lebanon areas and guerrilla shelling of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone wounds a civilian and a Lebanese policeman.
